facts.text: Detection identifies that an object is present, classification identifies its type, and tracking follows the object over time to determine where it is going; the results form an object list.
facts.quote: Detection says "something is there", classification says "it is a person" or "it is a truck", and tracking follows the object over time so the system knows where it is going; the result is written down as an object list.

facts.text: An object list contains one row per object with position relative to the machine, speed, class and confidence.
facts.quote: The object list is a table with one row per object: position relative to the machine, speed, class, confidence.

facts.text: Braking logic reads the object list rather than the raw image.
facts.quote: The braking logic reads this list, not the raw image.

facts.text: Hand-made object lists provide a test interface for decision logic and are the cheapest way to sweep many scenarios, but these tests provide no evidence that perception works.
facts.quote: It is a test interface: decision logic can be tested with hand-made object lists, the cheapest way to sweep many scenarios, but this says nothing about whether perception works [Chapter 7].

facts.text: Recording only object lists on the current fleet is a common mistake: without the raw data, new perception algorithms cannot be tested on those recordings.
facts.quote: Recording only object lists on the current fleet is a common mistake, because the raw data are gone and no new perception algorithm can ever be tested on them [Chapter 7].

facts.text: Object categories should be risk-based because braking depends on object vulnerability and whether the object is in the swept path, rather than whether a network labels the object as a person, vehicle or object.
facts.quote: the object categories should be risk-based: braking depends on how vulnerable the object is and whether it is in the swept path, not on whether a network says "person", "vehicle" or "object" [Chapter 9].

facts.text: One mining specification requires tracking six or more machines simultaneously.
facts.quote: One mining specification asks that six or more machines be tracked at once [Chapter 3].

facts.text: The existing warning system's baseline is measured as detections per encounter, broken down by object class, distance and condition, with track persistence included as one measure.
facts.quote: The baseline for the existing warning system is measured as detections per encounter by object class, distance and condition, with track persistence as one measure [Chapter 7]

facts.text: Checking a simulator only at the tracking output can conceal large errors in raw data.
facts.quote: a simulator checked only at the tracking output can hide large raw-data errors [Chapter 6].
